title: Getting Started: Setting Up the Time, Space, and Tools
coreMove: Stage enough time, space, and ordinary tools to make capturing and clarifying commitments frictionless before you try to work the system

exampleSpecs.domain: a public defender preparing for a Friday morning case-backlog reset
exampleSpecs.audience: an attorney whose desk is buried under hearing notices, client letters, and sticky-note promises
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether court deadlines and client follow-ups remain scattered in memory or enter a place that can be reviewed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the attorney protects a setup block, clears a real work surface, and chooses simple trays and folders instead of treating a new tool as the solution

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school theater director two weeks before opening night
exampleSpecs.audience: a teacher juggling rehearsal notes, parent emails, costume problems, and facility requests
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether dozens of small production commitments keep interrupting rehearsal because they have no single landing place
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director explains to a stage manager that the goal is not a prettier notebook but one reliable inbox where every loose commitment waits to be clarified

exampleSpecs.domain: a household with two preschoolers during a Sunday evening kitchen reset
exampleSpecs.audience: a parent who finds bills, permission slips, library notices, and repair reminders in six rooms
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether home administration keeps surfacing as background anxiety during meals, bedtime, and work calls
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the parent moves scattered paper and notes into one visible household inbox and names the relief as trust in a container, not improved willpower

exampleSpecs.domain: a touring cellist unpacking after a regional concert weekend
exampleSpecs.audience: a freelance musician whose commitments are made in hallways, cars, green rooms, and text threads
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether travel receipts, booking promises, repertoire notes, and payment questions disappear between cities
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the cellist identifies the failure as missing portable capture tools and a review point, not as being disorganized or unserious

exampleSpecs.domain: a community clinic charge nurse setting up a small admin corner before accreditation week
exampleSpecs.audience: a nurse responsible for shift coverage, supply requests, compliance reminders, and patient-call follow-ups
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether operational commitments get mixed with clinical urgency until everything feels equally loud
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the nurse creates a modest control center with an inbox, calendar access, reference space, and action lists while avoiding any sense that the setup itself is the achievement

exampleSpecs.domain: a neighborhood soccer coach using the trunk of a car as the season command post
exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer coach coordinating field permits, snack rotation, equipment, parent messages, and weather changes
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether preventable logistics keep stealing attention from practices and games
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coach tests whether each tool has a job—capture, hold, remind, or store—so the setup stays practical rather than becoming gear collecting
